scope: Proposition 6.1 of the manuscript “Nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation” (preprints/Nonuniqueness-for-the-periodic-hard-sphere-Boltzmann-equation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 363 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9cf0253f6b105302), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 28-29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix T ∈ (0, T0]. Either the zero-seed approximations of Proposition 5.1, or any sequence of its cap shots on [0, T], has a subsequence whose total densities FN = cN + hN converge weakly in L1([0, T] × Ω) to a nonnegative density F. The subsequence can be chosen so that FN (t) ⇀ F(t) in L1(Ω) at every t ∈ [0, T], with uniformly small polynomially weighted velocity tails. The limit has the common initial datum (4.4), and Q± (F, F) ∈ L1 ([0, T] × Ω), F ∈ C([0, T]; L1 (Ω)). 28 It satisfies every condition of Definition 2.1 on this interval, including the inequalities at every time. Each such limit has an admissible global continuation. The dormant upper bound, consisting of the cold majorants of Proposition 4.4 and t2H, passes to a zero-seed limit.
